title: Universe Timeline + Era Explorer
subtitle: 20 key moments from the Big Bang to today with quick encyclopedia jumps

eras.name: Early Universe
eras.summary: From quantum foam and inflation through recombination and the first hints of light.

eras.name: Stars
eras.summary: Ignition of Population III stars, heavy-element forging, and peak star birth.

eras.name: Galaxies
eras.summary: Protogalaxies merge, the cosmic web sharpens, and the Milky Way settles.

eras.name: Solar System
eras.summary: The Sun, planets, moons, and small bodies form from a protoplanetary disk.

eras.name: Life
eras.summary: Earth’s biosphere evolves from microbes to humans and a spacefaring civilization.

timeline.title: Planck era
timeline.description: Gravity and quantum mechanics share the stage at unimaginable energies. Space-time is frothy and seeds the tiny fluctuations everything else builds on.

timeline.title: Cosmic inflation ignites
timeline.description: Space expands exponentially faster than light, smoothing the cosmos. Quantum ripples balloon to cosmic scales that will become galaxies and voids.

timeline.title: Matter wins over antimatter
timeline.description: Tiny imbalances during cooling leave one extra matter particle per billion. Quark-gluon soup condenses toward protons and neutrons that survive annihilation.

timeline.title: Big Bang nucleosynthesis
timeline.description: The young universe forges its first elements: mostly hydrogen and helium with a dash of lithium. Fusion stops once expansion cools the fireball.

timeline.title: Matter grabs the wheel
timeline.description: Matter’s gravity overtakes radiation pressure, letting structures grow. Dark matter clumps deepen the wells that will guide galaxy formation.

timeline.title: Atoms form, light escapes
timeline.description: Electrons pair with protons, clearing the primordial fog. The cosmic microwave background streams out as the first baby picture of the universe.

timeline.title: Cosmic dark ages
timeline.description: Neutral hydrogen fills space with no stars yet to shine. Gravity quietly amplifies tiny ripples while the universe waits for ignition.

timeline.title: First stars ignite
timeline.description: Massive Population III stars burn hot and fast, emitting fierce ultraviolet light. Their supernovae seed space with the first heavy elements.

timeline.title: First galaxies assemble
timeline.description: Small protogalaxies merge inside dark-matter halos during the cosmic dawn. Gas flows create turbulent disks that start looking like spirals.

timeline.title: Reionization completes
timeline.description: Radiation from young galaxies and quasars strips electrons from hydrogen. The universe turns transparent again and stays ionized thereafter.

timeline.title: Cosmic web sharpens
timeline.description: Filaments feed galaxies while clusters condense at their nodes. Dark matter and hot gas trace the scaffolding that shapes where stars will form.

timeline.title: Cosmic noon starburst
timeline.description: The universe reaches its peak star-formation rate, making most existing stars. Supernova winds enrich and regulate growing galaxies.

timeline.title: Milky Way disk settles
timeline.description: Major mergers slow and our barred spiral stabilizes. A calm, star-forming disk and quiet halo emerge around Sagittarius A*.

timeline.title: Solar system forms
timeline.description: A collapsing nebula births the Sun and a rotating disk of dust. Planetesimals collide to build planets, moons, asteroids, and comets.

timeline.title: Life sparks on Earth
timeline.description: Microbes emerge in warm oceans soon after the crust cools. Biology begins reshaping the atmosphere and cycling elements.

timeline.title: Great Oxidation event
timeline.description: Photosynthetic microbes flood the air with oxygen, transforming oceans and rocks. Many anaerobic organisms perish while new metabolisms thrive.

timeline.title: Cambrian biodiversity boom
timeline.description: Multicellular life diversifies with eyes, shells, and limbs. Complex marine ecosystems appear, setting blueprints for future animals.

timeline.title: Age of dinosaurs
timeline.description: Continents shift and climates swing while reptiles rule land and sea. Flowering plants emerge and reshape ecosystems before a dramatic end.

timeline.title: Mammals and humans rise
timeline.description: After the impact, mammals radiate into new niches and brains grow. Homo sapiens emerge in Africa, mastering tools, language, and migration.

timeline.title: Space age to present
timeline.description: Sputnik opens orbit, Apollo reaches the Moon, and probes span the solar system. Hubble and JWST reveal first light as humanity maps the cosmos in detail.
